instruction: In VLC preferences, disable the option that forces VLC to use only one instance when files are opened from the file manager.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

llm_judge_reasons: The getter (get_vlc_config) correctly reads the vlcrc config file from the VM, which is where VLC persistently stores all preferences including the one-instance-when-started-from-file setting.

The metric (check_one_instance_when_started_from_file) correctly accesses rule['expected_one_instance_when_started_from_file'] directly from the rules dict — proper handling of expected.type='rule' parameter passing.
The expected value of 0 semantically matches the instruction requirement to 'disable' the option (0 = disabled in VLC config).
The default fallback in the metric code is '1' (enabled), ensuring the initial state correctly fails the evaluation — good negative control resistance.
Coverage is complete: the instruction has a single requirement (disable the one-instance setting) and the evaluator checks exactly that one config key.
No postconfig is needed because the getter reads from the persisted config file rather than from live UI state.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric does not skip comment lines (lines starting with '#'). In vlcrc, commented defaults like '#one-instance-when-started-from-file=1' contain the target substring and would match. In practice this is safe because VLC writes explicit uncommented lines when settings change and the loop's last-match-wins behavior lets the explicit setting override, but adding 'if line.startswith("#"): continue' would make the logic more robust.
